title: ΔΔCt and reference genes
objective: Explain why qPCR needs a reference gene and how ΔΔCt normalizes.

steps.title: You loaded different amounts
steps.body: No two samples have exactly the same amount of cDNA. A **[[reference gene]]** (a gene assumed steady across your conditions, like *Actb* or *Gapdh*) acts as a yardstick: you compare your gene of interest *to it*, cancelling out loading differences.

items: Measure Ct of your gene and the reference, each sample
ΔCt = gene Ct − reference Ct (normalize loading)
ΔΔCt = treated ΔCt − control ΔCt (compare conditions)
steps.explanation: First normalize to the reference within a sample, then compare across conditions, then convert to fold change.

steps.scenario: You loaded equal cDNA, yet your 'reference' gene's own Ct shifts a lot between control and treated groups.
options: The reference isn't stable here, so normalization is invalid
Nothing, since ΔΔCt already cancels out any reference shift
The target primers are failing, not the reference gene itself
steps.explanation: A reference must be unchanged by your treatment. If it moves, every normalized value is distorted. Validate references per experiment (a MIQE point).
steps.followUp: Fix: test several candidate references and use ones stable in *your* conditions, ideally more than one.

variants.prompt: A reference gene that changes with treatment is…
options: Invalid — it ends up biasing the normalization
Fine, since ΔΔCt cancels out the change anyway
Fine, as long as every sample uses the same one
variants.explanation: References must be stable across your conditions.

steps.prompt: Why normalize to a reference gene at all?
options: To cancel out differences in the amount of input cDNA
To correct for primer efficiency differences between genes
To convert Ct values into absolute mRNA copy numbers
To remove genomic DNA contamination from the signal
steps.explanation: Normalization removes loading/input differences so a change reflects biology, not pipetting.

variants.setup: Two samples had different cDNA input.
variants.prompt: What fixes that in the analysis?
options: Normalizing the data to a stable reference gene
Running more cycles so both samples plateau
Comparing the raw target Ct values directly
variants.reveal: Dividing by a steady reference cancels input differences.

sources.citation: Bustin SA et al., 2009, Clin Chem
sources.note: MIQE guidelines: rigorous qPCR, reference genes, reporting.
